bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds (INR 74.45 Cr) primarily deployed for capex (INR 57 Cr allocated) and general corporate purposes (INR 10.42 Cr); Working capital funded via bank limits (~8.15% interest rate); No dividend announced, focus on reinvestment.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Forex volatility (100% raw material import exposure); Geopolitical tensions affecting shipping costs (though routes currently clear); Raw material price fluctuations (West African crop dependency); Execution risk on new plant commissioning (Nov-Dec FY27 trial).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on operational moat (farm-gate sourcing) and tech upgrades; Pragmatic on margin pressures (temporary forex impact); Aggressive on capacity expansion timeline; Cautious on brand spend (margin-accretive growth only).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Tech upgrade in Nov-2023 (shelling/color sorters) drove kernel recovery ratio improvement and reduced contamination, fundamentally altering cost structure before IPO; 70:30 whole-to-broken ratio achieved is a key profitability lever; India's 30-35% global consumption share creates a massive import-substitution runway.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Origin-level sourcing network built over more than a decade across seven African cashew-producing countries (Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Ghana, Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau, Tanzania, Togo), giving visibility, flexibility and supply continuity through export-policy, freight and supply disruptions
- Backward-integrated consumer brand: unlike asset-light dry-fruit brands that buy from the market, Royal Mewa is fed by the Company's own sourcing, processing and quality controls, giving consistency and traceability
- Processing technology depth - advanced shelling and colour-sorting equipment sourced from Vietnam lifted kernel recovery, reduced contamination and sharpened product consistency
- Four-channel go-to-market (wholesale, institutional, branded consumer, export) spreading dependence across differing demand and margin profiles
- Proximity of facilities to Andhra Pradesh producing regions, lowering inbound logistics cost and transport emissions
- Full-value extraction from the raw material through by-products (shells, husk, powder), which contribute 4.69% of revenue
- Supplier diversification ratio of 74%, reducing procurement concentration risk
- Certification stack (ISO 9001, ISO 22000, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, HACCP, Halal, FSSAI) underpinning access to institutional and export customers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw cashew nut (RCN) price volatility — Explicitly identified by the Board as a key area of focus. RCN is the dominant input for a single-commodity processor, so swings in its price compress spreads directly. Mitigated through agile, real-time procurement, close alignment between sourcing and sales, and prudent working capital management.
- Foreign exchange fluctuation on cross-border trade — Named by the Board as an inherent aspect of the Company's cross-border model, with roughly 74-75% of sourcing imported and exports part of the channel mix. Managed through natural hedging and balanced exposure across procurement and sales geographies rather than through derivative hedging.
- Supply chain disruption and dependence on African sourcing origins — The Company procures Raw Cashew Nuts from seven African countries and imports supply 74-75% of its requirement, so evolving export policies, freight swings and origin-level supply disruption directly threaten continuity. Addressed through diversified sourcing, long-standing origin relationships, a widening independent supplier base (74% supplier diversification ratio) and robust logistics planning.
- Single-commodity and single-product concentration — Revenue is overwhelmingly cashew kernels; Royal Mewa contributes 1.68% and by-products 4.69% of revenue, so diversification away from the core commodity is still marginal. A structural downturn in cashew demand or realisations has no meaningful offset elsewhere in the portfolio.
- Single-site manufacturing concentration — All processing runs from one facility in Anakapalli, Andhra Pradesh, which operated at close to 86% utilisation through the year. Any interruption at that site halts output, and the Vizianagaram build is explicitly framed as bringing geographic diversification and operational resilience - which means that resilience does not yet exist.
- Execution risk on the Vizianagaram expansion — The greenfield facility is intended to nearly triple capacity from 18,000 MTPA towards 53,000 MTPA and absorbs Rs 57 crores of the Rs 74.45 crores IPO proceeds, with Rs 39.53 crores of purchase orders already issued. No commissioning date is disclosed, and the stated export ambition across nine international markets is conditioned on the facility being commissioned, so delay or cost overrun would defer both the capacity and the export strategy.
- Channel concentration in wholesale distribution — Distributors accounted for 65.21% of revenue in FY26, down from 80.42% in FY24 as institutional share rose to 33.96%. The wholesale channel still anchors revenue and plant utilisation, so distributor-level demand or credit stress transmits quickly to the plant.
- Statutory auditor discontinuity and governance transition — M/s Maheshwari & Co., appointed for a five-year term from 1 April 2025, resigned with effect from 19 June 2026 because the signing partner was surrendering his Certificate of Practice, requiring appointment of a replacement at an EGM on 16 July 2026. The Company also saw multiple board changes within the year (an Independent Director resigning 17 May 2025 and an Executive Director resigning 5 September 2025), which for a recently listed company is a governance-continuity risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Incorporated in September 2021, the Company processes, adds value to and markets cashew nut kernels, sourcing Raw Cashew Nuts from seven African origins and from Andhra Pradesh and processing them through automated shelling, drying, peeling, grading and sorting. It sells graded kernels to wholesale distributors, institutional customers (retailers, food processors and HoReCa) and export markets, and monetises by-products such as shells, husk and cashew powder. Royal Mewa, launched in 2024, is its consumer dry-fruit brand spanning cashews, almonds and pistachios.

- **By-products:** Cashew shells (biomass fuel / CNSL feedstock), Cashew husk (compost, mulch, animal bedding), Cashew powder (CP, food ingredient)

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No multi-year contracts; institutional clients provide 1-3 month visibility; 78% revenue from repeat customers indicating strong demand visibility rather than contractual backlog.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Greenfield expansion to 70k MT by FY30 (from 18k MT); Entry into quick commerce (Blinkit/Zepto); Potential re-entry into export markets (US/EU) post-FY28 once new capacity stabilizes; Backward integration into Indian sourcing to mitigate import risks.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale the processing base through the greenfield Vizianagaram facility, taking capacity from 18,000 MTPA towards 53,000 MTPA and giving geographic diversification and operational resilience within Andhra Pradesh
- Run a two-engine model in which the processing business creates volume and cash flow while Royal Mewa creates brand value and margin, the manufacturing base funding the patient build-out of the consumer brand
- Build Royal Mewa into a value engine riding the shift from loose and unbranded dry fruit to packaged, premium and traceable product, using sourcing and processing depth that an asset-light buy-from-the-market brand cannot match
- Grow Royal Mewa through carefully chosen retail, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels on the principle that brand visibility is never bought at the cost of margin
- Deepen the African procurement network and diversify suppliers so sourcing continuity is a strategic differentiator against export-policy shifts, freight swings and supply disruption
- Pursue operational excellence through process optimisation, quality-led manufacturing, modern sorting systems and automation, aiming for a manufacturing platform that delivers efficiency, scalability and sustainable profitability rather than volume alone
- Extend market access by strengthening channel partnerships with institutional customers, distributors and retail channels across established and emerging markets
- Invest technology and automation - advanced shelling, modern colour sorting and precision quality control - to lift yield and consistency at scale
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's expansion centres on a single greenfield project: a second cashew processing facility at Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh, on a site of 7,73,190 sq ft. Land was acquired during FY 2025-26, construction is advancing and machinery has been specified and is being sourced. The facility is stated to add 35,000 MT of processing capacity, taking the total from 18,000 MT towards 53,000 MT, and to bring geographic diversification and operational resilience alongside the existing Anakapalli plant. It is funded principally from the December 2025 BSE SME listing, which raised Rs 74.45 crores, of which Rs 57 crores is being deployed into land development, civil construction and the installation of advanced machinery; by the close of FY 2025-26 purchase orders worth Rs 39.53 crores had been issued against this plan with Rs 10.47 crores advanced. A further Rs 10.43 crores was earmarked for general corporate purposes, focused on the Royal Mewa brand, working capital and business development. The plant will carry advanced shelling, modern colour-sorting and precision quality-control equipment intended to lift yield and consistency, and will incorporate the effluent, sewage treatment, water-softening and reverse-osmosis infrastructure used at the existing facility, together with a creche, canteen and occupational health centre. The existing Anakapalli facility was itself expanded to 18,000 MTPA during FY 2025-26, from an initial 7,000 MTPA on acquisition in 2021, and ran at close to 86% utilisation through the year. No commissioning or ramp date for Vizianagaram is disclosed anywhere in the routed text. Export ambition is tied to the project: the Company aims to establish a presence across nine international markets across the Middle East, Asia, Europe and Southeast Asia following its commissioning.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is the world's largest cashew-consuming nation, accounting for over 30% of global kernel consumption, with annual domestic demand of approximately 4,25,000 MT
- Structural shift in Indian dry-fruit and nut consumption from loose and unbranded to packaged, premium and traceable product, spreading beyond metros into Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns
- E-commerce expansion carrying organised brands well past the metros and putting premium brands within reach of small towns
- India's branded dry-fruit and nut market estimated at around USD 2.24 billion in 2025 and projected to grow at a high single-digit annual rate over the coming decade (company cites an external market source)
- Premiumisation of the festive gifting economy, with consumers moving past generic hampers towards branded, presented products
- Growing taste for healthier snacking, bringing dry fruit into everyday habits rather than festive occasions alone
- Food processing sector gaining from rising health awareness, growing premium-food consumption, expanding organised retail and evolving consumer preferences
- Management view that the food processing industry is entering a phase where scale, quality, reliability and trust define competitive advantage, and that the opportunity ahead is materially larger than the one served so far
- Capacity utilisation of close to 86% at the Andhra Pradesh facility achieved before expansion benefits reach the business, which management cites as the basis for confidence in the period ahead
- Global cashew industry volatility during the year from evolving export policies, freight swings and supply disruptions, absorbed through diversified sourcing
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Pajson Agro delivered strong top-line growth (37% YoY) driven by tech-led yield improvements and distribution expansion, though H2 margins compressed to ~11% due to forex headwinds and IPO costs. The strategic pivot lies in the upcoming 35k MT greenfield facility (FY27-28) targeting automated efficiency and a high-margin B2C brand push, aiming to normalize EBITDA at 15-16% despite global sourcing risks.
